name: core/tie-is-insertion-order
why: Declared c, a, b and all priority 0: the batch must come back c, a, b. Alphabetical order, a hash order and a set order would each give something else, so this case makes insertion order observable rather than coincidental.

name: core/refuse/cycle-with-a-tail
why: The scan starts at `tail`, which is NOT in the cycle. What must come back is the cycle b -> c -> b, with the tail that only led into it trimmed off (ruling R2).

expected.reason: the graph has a cycle: b -> c -> b

name: core/refuse/first-cycle-in-input-order
why: Two disjoint cycles: input order decides which is named (ruling R1). y1 is declared first, so y1 -> y2 -> y1 is the answer and z1 -> z2 -> z1 is not.

expected.reason: the graph has a cycle: y1 -> y2 -> y1

name: core/refuse/walk-skips-emitted-dependencies
why: The walk follows only UN-EMITTED dependencies (ruling R1). x depends on root, which IS emitted, and on y, which is not: a walk that followed root would dead-end on a graph that does have a cycle.

expected.reason: the graph has a cycle: x -> y -> x

name: adversarial/priority/integer-literal-past-double-range
why: J85-R F1: the INTEGER spelling of a number past the double range. JSON.parse reads it as Infinity, so Number.isInteger is false; Python's json reads it as an exact int, which the planner must still refuse. 1e400 parses as a float in Python and never reaches that path.

expected.reason: nodes[0].priority must be an integer
